# 🏔️ The Lost Mine of Whisperhollow
### *What Was Sealed Below Was Never Meant to Be Forgotten*

---

The crumpled letter still sits in your vest pocket, Bramble — ink faded, paper soft with handling. You've read it a dozen times since it arrived at the Crossroads trading post three days ago:

> *"To any brave souls willing to answer — I am Brenna Stonemantle, elder of Whisperhollow. The earth shakes beneath us every night. Our livestock will not graze near the old mine. Three of our people went to investigate two weeks past and have not returned. I offer what coin our village can gather. Please. Come quickly, before there is no village left to save."*

The pay is meager. The danger, unknown. But a job's a job — and the trading post was getting a little *too* familiar with your face for comfort.

You weren't the only one who answered the call.

---

*The road narrows as you climb into the valley, the mountains pressing close on either side like the walls of a corridor. Late afternoon sunlight slants gold through the pine canopy overhead, and the air grows cooler with every step. Your five companions walk with you — a strange company thrown together by circumstance and a shared willingness to walk toward trouble.*

**Drak** leads the way in silence, as usual. His grey eyes scan the treeline while Talon circles overhead, a rust-red speck against the pale sky. The ranger hasn't said more than twenty words since you left the trading post, but his hand hasn't left his sword hilt either. 🦅

**Pip** walks beside you, close enough that your shoulders nearly brush — fellow halflings in a world built for taller folk. He's been humming a tune for the last mile and carrying the faint smell of wild herbs he picked along the trail. "You know what this valley needs?" he says brightly. "A good bakery. I can tell just by the soil — perfect for rye." 🍞

**Eldon** is three steps behind, muttering to himself and scribbling in a tiny notebook without looking up. The bronze beetle on his shoulder whirs and clicks. "— mineral deposits consistent with pre-Sundering geological surveys, which would *suggest* — oh! Did anyone else notice the quartz veining in that last outcrop? Fascinating stratification patterns, absolutely *fascinating* —" 🔧

**Sister Mirael** moves at the edge of the path, one hand trailing along the bark of passing trees. She hasn't said much, but you've caught her frowning at the forest floor, as if listening to something troubling in the earth. 🌿

And **Vaelith** brings up the rear, her plum cloak swept dramatically over one shoulder despite the lack of audience. "Charming," she drawls, surveying the valley. "Remote, impoverished, and *haunted.* I do so love a working holiday, darlings." ✨

---

*Whisperhollow reveals itself gradually — first a crumbling stone wall, then scattered cottages with dark windows, and finally a modest village square dominated by an ancient well. The only sign of life is a weathered tavern called the **Pickaxe & Pint**, its swinging sign creaking in the mountain breeze.*

*From somewhere deep in the earth beneath your feet, you feel more than hear a low, rhythmic vibration — like the heartbeat of the mountain itself.* 💓

The sun is setting. Warm light and the murmur of anxious voices spill from the tavern's open door. Up the hillside beyond the village, you can just make out the dark outline of massive iron doors set into the mountainside — the sealed mine entrance.

Drak pauses at the edge of the square. Grunts. "...Quiet. Too quiet for a village this size."

Pip's humming has stopped. His smile hasn't, but his eyes have gone sharp and watchful.

---

**Welcome to Whisperhollow, Bramble.** 🏘️⛏️

What would you like to do? You could:
- 🍺 **Head into the Pickaxe & Pint** to meet the locals and gather information
- 🏔️ **Investigate the mine entrance** up the hillside before dark
- 👀 **Take a careful look around the village square** first
- Or anything else that strikes your fancy!

The night is coming, and the mountain is humming. What's your move?
I go into the tavern, and sing a song about saving the town.

A bold entrance! Let me see how your performance lands with the nervous locals. Since you're singing to impress, that's a **Charisma (Performance) check**. You're not proficient in Performance, so it's just your Charisma modifier (+2).

🎲 **Performance Check:** d20 (16) + 2 CHA = **18** — A fine showing!

---

You push through the tavern door with the confidence of someone who's talked their way out of worse situations than a haunted mine. The Pickaxe & Pint is exactly what you'd expect — low ceilings, rough-hewn timber, the smell of hearth smoke and stale ale. A faded map of tunnels hangs behind the bar. Maybe a dozen villagers are clustered at tables, nursing drinks with the wide-eyed look of people who haven't slept well in weeks.

Every head turns as six strangers walk in.

Before the silence can get uncomfortable, you hop up onto the nearest empty table, pull yourself to your full three-foot-two, flash that crooked grin of yours, and *sing.*

It's not a song anyone here has heard before — because you're making it up on the spot. Something jaunty and swaggering about brave heroes come to set things right, with a rousing chorus about how *the dark below will tremble* and *the light will find its way.* Your voice isn't exactly bardic, but there's a rogue's charm in the delivery — cocky, winking, infectious.

🎵 *"So raise your cups, you Whisperhollow folk,*
*Don't you worry 'bout the dark below!*
*We've come to find what shakes your bones,*
*And send it packing down the road!"* 🎵

By the second verse, Pip is clapping along, beaming like a proud uncle. A few of the younger villagers crack reluctant smiles. An old woman near the fire actually *laughs* — a short, surprised sound, like she'd forgotten she could.

Even Vaelith arches an eyebrow from the doorway. "Well," she murmurs to Mirael. "He's certainly not *shy*, is he, darling?"

Mirael says nothing, but one corner of her mouth twitches. 🌿

Drak has already found a wall to lean against, eyes on the exits. Talon ruffles on his shoulder. Classic Drak.

---

As the song ends and a smattering of applause fills the room, a **stout, silver-haired dwarven woman** rises from a corner table. She wears a simple apron over practical clothes, and her fingers unconsciously find a worn holy symbol tucked into her belt. Her eyes are tired but sharp — and right now, they're fixed on you with a mixture of hope and wariness.

**"Well sung, little one,"** she says, her voice carrying the weight of someone used to being listened to. **"I am Brenna Stonemantle. I sent the letter."** She looks over your company — the scarred ranger, the chattering gnome, the quiet elf, the flamboyant tiefling, the cheerful monk, and you, still standing on her table. **"I prayed to Moradin that someone would answer. I did not expect... such a colorful answer."**

From the bar, a grizzled old man with a wild grey beard slams his mug down. 🍺

**"Bah!"** he growls. **"Songs won't save us, Brenna! That mine is** ***cursed.*** **My brother's bones are in there — forty years gone — and now whatever killed him is waking up! Mark my words, sending more folk down there is just feeding the beast!"** He jabs a gnarled finger at your group. **"You lot will end up like Haldor, Miri, and young Tam. Gone. Just** ***gone.***"

The room goes quiet again. The fire crackles.

Brenna's jaw tightens. "That is Old Tormund," she says, not unkindly. "He has... strong opinions."

Pip hops up beside you on the table and speaks quietly, his voice warm but steady: "That's a lot of fear in one room, friend. Might be worth hearing what both of them have to say, yeah?"

Eldon has already drifted toward the faded map behind the bar, brass goggles pulled down over his eyes. "Is that — yes, yes, a *tunnel survey!* Pre-closure cartography, if I'm not mistaken. The scale is off, but the basic topology —"

---

**The tavern is yours, Bramble.** 🍺⛏️

You've got the room's attention and two very different perspectives in front of you. What do you want to do?

- 🗣️ **Talk to Brenna** about the mine, the missing villagers, and what she knows
- 😤 **Engage Old Tormund** and try to get the real story behind his fear
- 🗺️ **Check out that map** behind the bar with Eldon
- 💬 **Work the room** — chat up the other villagers for rumors
- Or something else entirely!

Good instinct — a rogue knows the best information comes from loose lips, not official speeches. Let me see how well you read the room.

**Charisma (Deception) or Charisma (Persuasion)?** You're a Criminal — working a crowd for information is more about getting people to talk without realizing how much they're saying. Let's call this a **Charisma (Deception) check** — your proficiency applies. That's +4.

🎲 **Deception Check:** d20 (9) + 4 = **13** vs DC 12 — **Success!** Just enough charm to get tongues wagging.

---

You hop down from the table with a wink to Brenna — *"We'll talk properly soon, I promise"* — and get to work doing what you do best: being *everybody's friend.*

It's an art, really. Buy a round here. Lean in with a sympathetic nod there. Ask about the crops, the weather, the sheep — and let the conversation drift, naturally, inevitably, toward the mine. You circulate through the Pickaxe & Pint like you were born here, your crooked grin and easy manner putting folk at ease just enough to forget they're talking to a stranger. 🍺

Meanwhile, your companions settle into their own rhythms:

Pip has found the tavern's kitchen — such as it is — and is already helping the barkeep's wife chop vegetables, chatting warmly about nothing at all. People relax around Pip. It's his gift. 🍲

Drak watches the door. Talon watches the window. Neither speaks. 🦅

Vaelith has produced a deck of cards from somewhere and is teaching a young farmhand a game that he is *definitely* losing. "Oh, bad luck, sweetheart. Another hand? Double or nothing?" 🃏

---

Here's what you piece together over the course of an hour:

📜 **What the villagers tell you:**

- **The tremors** started about a month ago. Small at first — rattling cups, spooking livestock. Now they come every night, strong enough to crack plaster. Always rhythmic. Always from beneath the mine. 💓

- **Three villagers went missing** two weeks ago: **Haldor** (a broad-shouldered farmer), **Miri** (his wife, the village herbalist), and **young Tam** (a twelve-year-old boy, Elara the shepherd's brother). They went to investigate on their own. Nobody's seen them since.

- **A young woman named Elara Windmere** — Tam's older sister — has been *furious* that Brenna won't let her go after them. She's apparently the best mountain guide in the valley. A few villagers point toward a corner table where a sun-browned young woman with keen hazel eyes sits alone, jaw clenched, staring into an untouched ale. 👩‍🌾

- **Most villagers believe the mine is cursed.** Tormund's been telling anyone who'll listen that the dead miners' spirits are angry. A few of the older folk remember the mine being sealed "practically overnight" forty years ago with no real explanation.

- **One detail catches your ear** — a quiet old shepherd leans in and mutters: *"Tormund says the mine killed his brother. But my da told me different. Said the miners who stayed behind... they* ***chose*** *to stay. Volunteered, like. Never made sense to me."* He shrugs and goes back to his ale.

That last bit is interesting. Miners who *volunteered* to be sealed inside? 🤔

---

Eldon, meanwhile, has been studying the faded map behind the bar with increasing excitement. He suddenly spins around, goggles askew, and announces to no one in particular:

"The tunnel system is *far* more extensive than surface geography would suggest! At least three main shafts, a junction complex at — oh, roughly two hundred feet down — and what appears to be a natural cavern system beyond that. And *look* at this mineral notation — unless I'm very much mistaken, that symbol indicates **starsteel** deposits. *Starsteel!* Do you have any idea how rare — how astronomically, impossibly rare —" He catches himself, clears his throat. "It's, ah. Interesting. Academically." 🔧✨

Sister Mirael has been standing near the open door, one hand resting on the frame. She speaks quietly, almost to herself:

"...The trees here are troubled. Their roots go deep, and something below... *hums* to them. Not a threat. More like... a heartbeat that has forgotten how to rest." 🌿

---

**The picture is forming, Bramble.** A sealed mine. Missing people. Tremors. And a forty-year-old secret that doesn't quite add up.

The evening is getting late. What's your next move?

- 👩‍🌾 **Talk to Elara Windmere** — she's clearly burning to act, and she knows these mountains
- 🛕 **Seek out Brenna privately** — she sent the letter, and she's holding something back
- 😤 **Corner Old Tormund** — his fear is real, but that story about volunteers doesn't match his version
- 🗺️ **Study the map with Eldon** and plan a route into the mine
- 🌙 **Call it a night** and head for the mine at first light
- Or something else!
I run outside yelling, into the mine!

You bolt for the tavern door, nearly knocking over a startled farmer and his ale. Pip's head snaps up from the kitchen. Drak pushes off the wall. Vaelith's card game freezes mid-deal.

**"Into the mine, friends! No time like the present!"** you shout over your shoulder, bursting into the cool mountain air.

The village square is dark now, lit only by the glow spilling from the tavern and a scattering of stars overhead. The sealed mine entrance looms up the hillside — two massive iron doors, barely visible in the moonlight, green with age. You can *feel* the vibration through your boots, stronger out here. Like standing on the chest of something breathing. 💓

You're halfway across the square when a firm hand catches your shoulder.

**"Bramble."** Drak's voice, low and flat. He's fast for a man in scale mail. Talon circles overhead, a dark shape against the stars. 🦅

"...Night. Unknown terrain. No plan." He looks up at the mine entrance, then back at you. "Saw the map. Tunnels collapse. Things *live* in there." A pause. "You want to die on an empty stomach?"

Pip jogs up beside you, slightly out of breath, still holding a half-peeled potato. "He's got a point, friend! Well — not about the stomach, I can fix that in twenty minutes — but more about the, ah, *charging headlong into a sealed haunted mine in the dark* part." He gives you that warm, dimpled grin, but his eyes are serious. "Those three villagers went in without a plan, and they haven't come back." 🥔

Vaelith arrives last, leaning against the well with studied nonchalance. "Oh, are we doing the *heroic suicide rush* already? I thought that was usually a day-two activity, darling." She examines her nails. "Besides, those doors are *sealed.* With dwarven wards. You were going to — what — knock politely?" ✨

Sister Mirael stands at the edge of the square, head tilted, listening. "...The earth's rhythm has not changed. Whatever stirs below has waited forty years." She turns her amber eyes to you. "It will wait one more night. But we should not wait longer than that." 🌿

Even Eldon has caught up, panting, notebook clutched to his chest. "Yes — and I *need* to study that tunnel map properly! There are at least three potential collapse zones I identified at a glance, and if those rune markings on the door are what I *think* they are, brute-forcing entry could trigger — well. Let's just say we'd rather *solve* the door than *break* it." 🔧

---

They've got a point, and your rogue instincts know it. Charging into an unknown dungeon at night with no reconnaissance is... well, it's how people become the next set of missing villagers. 💀

But the night is young yet, and there's still work to be done before dawn.

**What do you want to do, Bramble?**

- 🌙 **Fine, fine — head back inside** and use the evening wisely. Talk to Brenna or Elara before turning in.
- 🏔️ **At least scout the mine entrance** from the outside while you're out here — get a look at those doors and wards without going in.
- 😏 **Insist on going NOW** — you're a rogue, darkness is your element, and those missing people might not have another night.
- 💤 **Get some rest** — you'll need your strength. First light, you go in.
- Or something else entirely!
"Into the mine!" I remove my armor, out the door and into the mine

You shrug off your leather armor right there in the village square, letting it drop to the dirt. The cool mountain air hits your linen shirt as you flash that crooked grin at your stunned companions.

**"Lighter is faster, friends!"** And you're off, sprinting up the hillside toward the mine entrance, chestnut hair whipping in the night breeze. 🏃‍♂️💨

Behind you, chaos.

**"Bramble — !"** Pip drops the potato.

Drak swears under his breath — something in Orcish — and takes off after you, boots pounding the dirt. 🦅

**"Oh, wonderful. He's *actually* doing it."** Vaelith pushes off the well with a groan. "I am *not* running." She runs. ✨

Mirael and Eldon exchange a glance and follow.

---

You reach the mine entrance in under a minute, breathing hard, moonlight gleaming on the massive iron doors. Up close, they're *imposing* — ten feet tall, green with verdigris, banded with cold iron engraved with dwarven runes. The welds that sealed them shut decades ago are cracked and flaking. A thin draft of warm, mineral-scented air seeps through the gaps, and the vibration in the ground is *strong* here — a deep, resonant pulse that rattles your teeth. 💓

Three bedrolls and a shattered lantern lie at the base of the doors. The missing villagers' camp. They made it this far.

Now — the doors. They're sealed with dwarven wards, and the runes around the frame glow faint blue-silver in response to your approach. You're looking for a way in.

**Forcing them open would take a DC 18 Strength check** — not exactly your forte at +0. But you're a rogue. You look for *other* ways in.

Let's see if those sharp eyes spot anything useful. **Wisdom (Perception) check** — you're proficient, so that's +2.

🎲 **Perception Check:** d20 (13) + 2 WIS = **15** vs DC 12 — **Success!** 👀

Your rogue's eye catches it immediately: **faint blue-white light flickering behind the sealed doors**, pulsing in time with the vibrations beneath your feet. Something in there is *alive* — or at least active. And those cracks in the welds... they're not just age. Something has been pushing from the *inside*.

The others catch up, winded. Drak's hand is on his sword. Pip's smile is gone — replaced by that quiet, focused look he gets when things are serious.

**"Bramble."** Mirael's voice, soft but firm. She's looking at your bare arms, your unprotected chest. "You have shed your shell like a snake that does not yet have new skin. Whatever lies beyond those doors will not care about your speed if it finds your heart." 🌿

She's not wrong. Without your leather armor, **your AC drops from 14 to 11** (10 + 3 DEX, no armor). You're fast, but you're *exposed*.

Vaelith arrives last, slightly out of breath, cloak askew. She takes one look at the glowing runes and her golden eyes go wide. For just a moment, the performance drops. Then it's back. "Well, darling, if you're *quite* finished with your dramatic sprint — those are **dwarven ward sequences**. Eldon?"

Eldon pushes past everyone, goggles down, practically vibrating. "Yes — *yes!* A protective ward circuit! If I can trace the activation pattern — this is **Moradinian lock-craft**, I've read about this, the sequence follows the rhythm of the Soulforger's hammer strikes —"

---

**The moment of truth, Bramble.** ⛏️🚪

You're at the doors. Your armor is back in the village square. The night is dark and the mountain hums beneath you.

- 🔓 **Let Eldon try to solve the rune lock** — he seems to know what he's doing (Arcana check, DC 13)
- 💪 **Try to force the doors anyway** — maybe Drak can help (Strength DC 18, but he's got +2 STR)
- 🎒 **...Go back for your armor first.** Mirael has a point. Charging into a dungeon half-naked is how rogues become dead rogues.
- 🔍 **Search around the entrance** for another way in — a crack, a vent, a side passage
- 😏 **Something else?**

What do you do?
I run to the mine door and try my thief skills

Alright, you're going for it! Those nimble fingers have cracked plenty of locks before — let's see how they do against dwarven engineering that's been here for forty years.

You pull out your thieves' tools and crouch by the doors, examining the seams where the welds have cracked. The runes pulse blue-silver as your fingers brush the cold iron. This isn't a *normal* lock — there's no keyhole, no tumbler mechanism. But those cracked welds have created gaps, and where there are gaps, there are opportunities...

This is a **Dexterity (Thieves' Tools) check**. You have Expertise here, so that's double proficiency: +7. However, this isn't a conventional lock — it's dwarven ward-craft. I'll set the DC accordingly.

🎲 **Thieves' Tools Check:** d20 (10) + 7 = **17** vs DC 18 — **Failure.** 😬

---

Your picks slide into the gaps between the cracked welds. You probe, twist, feel for give — and for a moment, you think you've got something. A mechanism *shifts* deep inside the iron frame. A click. A second click.

Then the runes flare **bright red**. ❌🔴

A pulse of energy snaps through your picks like a static shock, numbing your fingers. You yank your hands back with a hiss.

**"Ow —** clever old dwarves..."

The doors don't budge. The runes fade back to their steady blue-silver glow, as if nothing happened. Your thieves' tools are fine, but your pride is bruised. Whatever's holding these doors shut, it isn't just *mechanical*. There's magic woven into the metalwork — the lock and the wards are one and the same.

Eldon practically *squeals* from behind you. "Oh — oh, *fascinating!* Did you see the resonance cascade in the secondary rune cluster? The ward interpreted your manipulation as an unauthorized intrusion attempt and redirected the kinetic energy back through the contact point — a *brilliant* failsafe, really. Pre-Sundering dwarven artificers were simply —"

**"Eldon."** Drak. One word. The gnome stops. 🔧

Pip crouches beside you, checking your hands. "Fingers still attached? Good. My gran always said, *some doors want a key, and some doors want a kind word.* Maybe this one's the second sort." 🍞

Vaelith leans in, studying the rune sequence with her golden eyes. "He's not entirely wrong, much as it pains me to admit. These wards aren't *hostile* — they're *protective.* They're asking for a password, not a fight, darling." ✨

Eldon is already bouncing on his toes. "Yes — YES! I was *trying* to say — this is a **Moradinian rune lock!** The activation sequence follows the pattern of the Soulforger's hammer strikes. If I can trace them in the correct order..." He looks at you, goggles gleaming in the moonlight. "May I?"

---

**The doors aren't giving up their secrets to lockpicks, Bramble.** 🚪🔒 This one needs magic or knowledge, not dexterity.

What's the call?

- 🔮 **Let Eldon try the rune sequence** — he's the expert here (Arcana check, DC 13)
- 💪 **Have Drak try to brute-force it** — the welds ARE cracked, after all (Athletics DC 18)
- 🎒 **Head back to the village** — maybe Brenna knows the passphrase. And your armor is still on the ground down there...
- 🤔 **Something else?**

You step back, shaking the tingle from your fingers, and give the gnome a nod. "All yours, Eldon."

**"Oh, splendid!"** He's already at the doors, tiny fingers tracing the rune sequence, muttering calculations at a speed that makes your head spin. The bronze beetle on his shoulder leans forward as if reading along. 🔧

"Right — so the primary sequence starts *here*, follows the descending hexagonal pattern — that's the first hammer strike — then loops back through the tertiary cluster — second strike — and if the Moradinian liturgical cadence holds true, the third strike should land... *here.*"

He presses three runes in rapid succession. **Arcana check**, with his +5 modifier:

🎲 **Arcana Check:** d20 (2) + 5 = **7** vs DC 13 — **Failure.** 😬

---

The runes flare **red** again. ❌🔴 Another pulse of energy — this time Eldon yelps and snatches his hands back, shaking them wildly. His goggles fly up off his face and land crooked on top of his copper hair.

"That — that's *not right.* The secondary resonance pattern should have — unless the liturgical cadence uses the *alternate* Moradinian meter, which would mean — oh. Oh, I may have been thinking of the *Gnomish* adaptation, not the original dwarven sequence. Entirely different rhythmic structure. Hmm." He pulls out his notebook and begins scribbling furiously. "I need *more data.*" 🔧📓

Vaelith slow-claps from behind. "Riveting performance, Sparky. Truly." ✨

Drak just looks at the doors, then up the mountainside, then back down at the village. "...Brenna knows something. You saw her hand go to that holy symbol when we walked in. She's carrying something she hasn't told us."

Mirael nods slowly. "...The seed does not grow until the soil is ready. She was not ready to trust us yet. But we have shown we are willing to act. Perhaps now she will speak." 🌿

Pip — who at some point retrieved your leather armor from the village square — holds it out to you with a cheerful smile. "Picked this up on the way, friend. Thought you might want it back before you catch your death. Or, you know, before something catches *you.*" 🍞

---

The doors stand firm. Two attempts, two failures. Whatever password or pattern opens this lock, you don't have it yet — and the night is getting colder.

But Drak's right. Brenna sent that letter for a reason. She *wants* help. And that nervous hand on her holy symbol, the shrine behind her cottage, the story about her grandmother sealing the mine... she's holding a piece of this puzzle. 🧩

**What's the play, Bramble?**

- 🎒 **Put your armor back on** and head down to talk to Brenna — time to earn her trust and get answers
- 👩‍🌾 **Find Elara Windmere instead** — Tam's sister might know another way into the mine
- 😤 **Try the doors one more time** — third time's the charm, right?
- 💤 **Call it a night** — rest up, talk to Brenna at first light with fresh eyes
- 🤔 **Something else?**

You take the armor from Pip with a sheepish grin. "...Thanks, Pip."

"Don't mention it, friend. Happens to the best of us." He winks. 🍞

You pull the leather armor back on as the group heads down the hillside toward the Pickaxe & Pint. The familiar weight settles across your shoulders — **AC back to 14**. Feels better already.

---

Inside the tavern, the crowd has thinned. Tormund has retreated to his corner, muttering into his beard. Brenna is deep in quiet conversation with the barkeep. And there, at a table alone near the back wall, sits **Elara Windmere**. 👩‍🌾

She's younger than you expected — early twenties, sun-browned skin, calloused hands wrapped around an untouched ale. Her hazel eyes are sharp and restless, darting to the door every few seconds. There's a shepherd's crook leaning against the wall behind her and a coil of rope at her feet. She came to the tavern *prepared*, like she's been waiting for an excuse to move.

You slide into the chair across from her. She looks you up and down — takes in the lockpicks at your belt, the scar across your nose, the eyes that are already cataloging the room's exits.

"You're one of the ones who answered Brenna's letter," she says. Not a question. Her voice is steady but tight, like a bowstring held too long. "I saw you run up the hill just now." A flicker of something — respect? Impatience? "At least *someone* around here wants to *do* something."

She leans forward, voice dropping. 

"My brother **Tam** is in that mine. He's *twelve*. He went in with Haldor and Miri two weeks ago because nobody else would, and Brenna won't let me go after him. Says it's too dangerous for one person." Her jaw tightens. **"She's right. That's why I need** ***you.***"

She glances around, then pulls something from inside her vest — a folded piece of leather, cracked with age. She spreads it on the table between you.

It's a **rough map of the mountain's eastern face**. Not the mine tunnels — the *outside*.

"I've herded sheep on this mountain my whole life. I know every ridge, every crack, every runoff channel." She taps a spot on the map. "There's a **ventilation shaft** here — old dwarven work, half-hidden by scrub. Comes out on the eastern slope about two hundred feet up. It's narrow, and I don't know where it connects to the main tunnels, but it's *open.* Air flows through it. I've felt it." 🗺️

She looks up at you, hazel eyes burning.

"The front doors are sealed with magic I don't understand. But this shaft? No runes. No wards. Just rock and darkness." She pauses. "It's a tight squeeze. Too tight for someone in heavy armor. But for someone your size..." She gives a pointed look at your halfling frame. "...it might just work."

Pip's ears perk up from the next table. He's been listening — of course he has. "Tight tunnels? That's halfling territory, that is." He grins, but there's steel underneath.

Drak appears at your shoulder. He studies the map for a long moment, then traces a line with one finger. "...Ventilation shaft. Connects to the upper tunnel network, most likely. Could bypass the sealed entrance entirely." He looks at Elara. "You can guide us to it?"

**"At first light,"** she says firmly. "The eastern slope is treacherous in the dark. But at dawn, I can have you there in an hour."

Vaelith peers over your shoulder at the map, one eyebrow raised. "A back door. How delightfully *sneaky.*" She glances at you. "I'm beginning to like this plan, darling." ✨
